This page uses the following **route convention**. Category O means the BGG
category for a fixed finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra and a
chosen positive system, as defined in [[def-bgg-category-o]]. The
Arakawa–Suzuki route is the *degenerate affine* route over $\mathbb C$: on
$M\otimes (\mathbb C^N)^{\otimes d}$ use the operators $x_j$ and $s_i$ of
[[def-arakawa-suzuki-casimir-operators-on-tensor-functors]], with the verified
right $H_d$-action of
[[thm-the-casimir-and-place-permutation-operators-satisfy-degenerate-affine-hecke-relations]].
The source-normalized operators are
$$y_j=x_j-\frac{1}{N}z_M+\frac{N-1}{2};$$
they are not new generators to be identified with a nondegenerate Hecke
generator. Here $z_M$ is the central endomorphism specified in the cited
definition. This convention asserts no extension of the cited hypotheses on
$M$, origin, or tensor functor.

The finite cyclic type-A Hecke/KLR route uses a field $F$, a finite quantum
characteristic $e\ge2$, and its declared residue and cyclotomic conventions
([[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]]). In the nondegenerate
branch write the Hecke parameter as $\xi\ne1$ and reserve $q$ for the grading
and Laurent-polynomial variable. The blockwise identification is exactly
[[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]]: write
$\xi_{\mathrm{BK}}$ for its Hecke parameter (denoted $q$ in that theorem),
independent of the grading variable $q$. Its $\xi_{\mathrm{BK}}=1$ branch
requires $\operatorname{char}F=e$, while its $\xi_{\mathrm{BK}}\ne1$ branch is
separate. For
level-one Ariki statements, use only the regime in
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]]. In characteristic
zero the canonical-basis and graded-decomposition conclusions are those of
[[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] and
[[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]].
In positive characteristic retain the adjustment factorization of
[[thm-positive-characteristic-decomposition-polynomials-factor-through-adjustment]];
no identity adjustment matrix is part of this route.

The negative-half KLR categorification and the cyclotomic highest-weight
projective-$K_0$ theorem are distinct routes, respectively
[[thm-klr-categorification-of-the-negative-quantum-half]] and
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]].
Each keeps its own field, grading, weight and Axiom-of-Choice hypotheses
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
Likewise, the type-A Hecke cellular result
[[thm-murphy-tableau-elements-form-a-cellular-basis]], the local type-A
character theorem [[thm-soergels-character-conjecture]], the singular spherical
formula [[thm-singular-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]],
and the regular-ambient parabolic antispherical formula
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]] retain
their distinct statements and ranges. This route convention introduces no
new theorem, grading, equivalence, or cross-characteristic transfer.

Work over $\mathbb C$ ([[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]],
[[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). Fix $N\ge1$, let
$\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ with its matrix units $E_{ij}$ and the
trace form $B(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}(XY)$, which is symmetric, nondegenerate and
invariant ([[prop-trace-forms-are-symmetric-and-invariant]]), and let
$$z:=\sum_{i=1}^NE_{ii}\in\mathfrak g$$
be the central element (the identity matrix). The dual basis of $(E_{ij})$
under $B$ is $(E_{ji})$, so the invariant Casimir tensor is
$$\Omega=\sum_{i,j=1}^NE_{ij}\otimes E_{ji}\in U(\mathfrak g)\otimes U(\mathfrak g),$$
Its action on a tensor product of two $\mathfrak g$-modules commutes with the diagonal action, as computed in [F2]. Multiplying its two factors gives the central Casimir element of [[def-casimir-operator-relative-to-an-invariant-form]].

Let $M$ be a $\mathfrak g$-module and $V=\mathbb C^N$ the natural module
([[def-representation-of-a-lie-algebra]]). On the tensor product
$M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]],
[[thm-associativity-of-balanced-tensor-products]]) label the factors
$0,1,\dots,d$, with factor $0$ equal to $M$. For $0\le a\ne b\le d$ let
$\Omega_{ab}$ denote the operator obtained by applying $\Omega$ in the two
labelled factors, and for distinct $1\le a,b\le d$ let $P_{ab}$ denote the
operator that interchanges the two labelled factors (the flip of
$V\otimes V$ on two $V$-factors). Define, for $1\le j\le d$ and
$1\le i\le d-1$,
$$x_j:=\Omega_{0j}+\sum_{k<j}P_{kj},\qquad s_i:=P_{i,i+1}.$$
Finally put $\Omega^{\mathrm{sl}}:=\Omega-\tfrac1Nz\otimes z$ and define the
Arakawa-Suzuki normalized operators
$$y_j:=x_j-\tfrac1Nz_M+\tfrac{N-1}{2},$$
where $z_M$ denotes the endomorphism of $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ given by the
action of $z$ on the factor $M$. This is a central endomorphism, and is a scalar only when $z$ acts scalarly on $M$.

The verification below records the properties of these operators used on this
page: $\Omega$ acts on $V\otimes V$ as the flip; the operators $x_j$ and
$s_i$ are natural in $M$ and commute with the $\mathfrak g$-action; the
recursion $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$ holds; $\Omega^{\mathrm{sl}}$ is the Casimir
of $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ relative to the restricted trace form; and the operators
$y_j$ are exactly the source operators of [AS, (2.2.2)]. For $d=0$ the family
$(x_j)$ is empty; for the trivial module $M=\mathbb C$ one has $\Omega_{0j}=0$,
so $x_j=\sum_{k<j}P_{kj}$ and $x_1=0$.

1. The operators $x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ commute with the
   $\mathfrak g$-action and are natural in $M$, and satisfy all the defining

   [[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]]: the Coxeter relations for the
   $s_i$; $s_ix_j=x_js_i$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$; $s_ix_{i+1}=x_is_i+1$ and

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

Every Verma module $M(\lambda)$, every quotient of it, and every finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module belongs to $\mathcal O$.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Let $\{\alpha_i\}_{i\in I}$ be the simple roots of the chosen positive system and write $Q^+=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$ and $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$. Let $W$ be the Weyl group of [[def-root-reflections-and-the-weyl-group-action]] and let $\rho$ be the Weyl vector of [[def-weyl-vector-rho-for-a-chosen-positive-system]]; for $w\in W$ set $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

The **BGG category $\mathcal O$** is the full subcategory of left $U(\mathfrak g)$-modules $M$ satisfying all three conditions: $M$ is finitely generated; $M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in\mathfrak h^*}M_\mu$ where $M_\mu=\{v:hv=\mu(h)v\text{ for all }h\in\mathfrak h\}$; and $U(\mathfrak n^+)v$ is finite dimensional for each $v\in M$. Its morphisms are all $\mathfrak g$-linear maps. The zero module is included, generated by the empty set. The enveloping and triangular conventions are those of [[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]] and [[thm-triangular-decomposition-from-a-chosen-positive-root-system]].

Work over the field $\mathbb C$ and fix an integer $d\ge 0$
([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], [[def-commutative-ring]]). Let
$\mathcal F_d$ be the free associative unital $\mathbb C$-algebra on the
$d+\max(d-1,0)$ symbols $x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ (for $d=0$ there is only
the unit; for $d=1$ only $x_1$), with its word basis and universal property
([[lem-hh-free-associative-ring-and-relations-descent]]), and let
$I_d\mathrel{\trianglelefteq}\mathcal F_d$ be the two-sided ideal
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]])
generated by the following elements:

- $x_ix_j-x_jx_i$ for all $1\le i,j\le d$;
- $s_i^2-1$ for $1\le i\le d-1$;
- $s_is_{i+1}s_i-s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1}$ for $1\le i\le d-2$;
- $s_is_j-s_js_i$ for $1\le i,j\le d-1$ with $|i-j|>1$;
- $s_ix_j-x_js_i$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$, $s_ix_{i+1}-x_is_i-1$, and
  $x_{i+1}s_i-s_ix_i-1$, for $1\le i\le d-1$ and $1\le j\le d$.

The **degenerate affine Hecke algebra** is the quotient $\mathbb C$-algebra
$$H_d:=\mathcal F_d/I_d$$
with unit element written $1$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]). We keep the symbols
$x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ for their images, and for $w\in S_d$ we write
$w$ for the image in $H_d$ of any word in the $s_i$ representing $w$; this is
independent of the chosen word once the basis theorem below is proved. For
$d\ge1$ and $a\in\mathbb C$, the notation $H_d/(x_1-a)$ means the quotient by the two-sided
ideal generated by $x_1-a$.

The verification below establishes exactly the structure of $H_d$ used
throughout this page: the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad r_1,\dots,r_d\ge0,\ w\in S_d,$$
form a $\mathbb C$-basis, so that
$H_d\cong\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[S_d]$ as a vector
space with polynomial and group-algebra subalgebras
([[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]], [[def-group-ring]]);
$H_0=\mathbb C$ and $H_1=\mathbb C[x_1]$; for $d\ge1$ and every $a$ there is a unique
algebra isomorphism
$$H_d/(x_1-a)\cong\mathbb C[S_d],\qquad x_j\longmapsto a+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j),\qquad s_i\longmapsto(i\ i+1);$$
and total polynomial degree is an algebra filtration whose associated graded is
the semidirect product $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$ in which
$s_i$ acts by swapping $x_i$ and $x_{i+1}$. For $d\ge2$, the cross relation is
inhomogeneous, so it does not turn $H_d$ into a graded algebra with
$\deg x_i=1$ and $\deg s_i=0$. For $d=0$ the algebra $\mathbb C$ has its
degree-zero grading, and for $d=1$ the algebra $\mathbb C[x_1]$ has its
natural polynomial grading.

Write $\mathfrak{gl}_2(\mathbb C)=M_2(\mathbb C)$ for the Lie algebra of
complex $2\times2$ matrices under the commutator bracket
$[A,B]=AB-BA$ ([[def-representation-of-a-lie-algebra]],
[[def-lie-algebra-over-a-field]]). The **special linear Lie algebra**
$\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$ is the Lie subalgebra
([[def-lie-subalgebra-ideal-and-center]]) of traceless matrices

$$\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)=\{A\in M_2(\mathbb C):\operatorname{tr}A=0\},$$

which is closed under the bracket because $\operatorname{tr}(AB-BA)=0$. Put

$$e=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad f=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad h=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

Direct matrix multiplication gives $he-eh=2e$, $hf-fh=-2f$ and
$ef-fe=h$, that is,

$$[h,e]=2e,\qquad [h,f]=-2f,\qquad [e,f]=h .$$

Since $\{e,f,h\}$ is a basis of the space of traceless matrices, these
relations determine the bracket completely, $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$ is
three-dimensional, and $h$ spans a one-dimensional abelian subalgebra.
A Lie algebra over $\mathbb C$ is called a **copy of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$** if it
has a basis $(e,f,h)$ satisfying exactly these three bracket relations.

Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field $k$.

- It is **simple** if it is nonabelian and its only ideals are $0$ and
  $\mathfrak g$.
- It is **semisimple** if
  $\operatorname{rad}(\mathfrak g)=0$, as in
  [[def-semisimple-lie-algebra-by-vanishing-radical]].
- When $\operatorname{char}k=0$, it is **reductive** when
  $$\mathfrak g=Z(\mathfrak g)\oplus[\mathfrak g,\mathfrak g]$$
  and the derived algebra $[\mathfrak g,\mathfrak g]$ is semisimple, as in
  [[def-reductive-lie-algebra-by-semisimple-derived-algebra-and-center]].

The word “nonabelian” in the first clause excludes one-dimensional abelian
Lie algebras from being simple. The zero Lie algebra is semisimple under the
vanishing-radical convention and, when $\operatorname{char}k=0$, is reductive,
with both displayed summands zero. These are conventions, not yet the structure theorem that every
semisimple algebra is a direct sum of simple ideals.

A finite-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ is **semisimple** if its
solvable radical vanishes:

$$\operatorname{rad}(\mathfrak g)=0.$$

Here the radical is the largest solvable ideal from
[[def-radical-of-a-finite-dimensional-lie-algebra]]. Under this convention the
zero Lie algebra is semisimple, because its radical is zero. A nonzero solvable
Lie algebra is not semisimple, since it equals its radical. No assertion about
decomposition into simple ideals is built into this definition; that
characterization requires later structure theory. The definition is valid over
any field and uses no choice principle.

Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra. Its **solvable
radical**, denoted $\operatorname{rad}(\mathfrak g)$, is the largest solvable
ideal of $\mathfrak g$: it is a solvable ideal and contains every solvable
ideal of $\mathfrak g$. Here solvability is as in
[[def-derived-series-and-solvable-lie-algebra]], and “ideal” has the meaning in
[[def-lie-subalgebra-ideal-and-center]].

Existence and uniqueness are not assumed merely from the phrase “largest.”
They are supplied by [[thm-sum-of-solvable-ideals-is-solvable]], which proves
that finite sums remain solvable and that finite dimensionality reduces the
sum of all solvable ideals to a finite sum.

Thus $\operatorname{rad}(0)=0$. If $\mathfrak g$ is solvable, then
$\operatorname{rad}(\mathfrak g)=\mathfrak g$; otherwise the radical may be
zero or a proper nonzero ideal. No characteristic assumption is made.

Let $\mathfrak g$ be a Lie algebra over a field ([[def-lie-algebra-over-a-field]]).
For linear subspaces $A,B\subseteq\mathfrak g$, write

$$
[A,B]=\operatorname{span}\{[a,b]:a\in A,\ b\in B\}.
$$

The **derived series** of $\mathfrak g$ is

$$\mathfrak g^{(0)}=\mathfrak g,\qquad \mathfrak g^{(r+1)}=[\mathfrak g^{(r)},\mathfrak g^{(r)}]\quad(r\geq0).$$

Each $\mathfrak g^{(r)}$ is an ideal ([[def-lie-subalgebra-ideal-and-center]]).
Indeed, if $I$ is an ideal, Jacobi gives

$$[x,[a,b]]=\bigl[ [x,a],b\bigr]+\bigl[a,[x,b]\bigr]\in[I,I]$$

for $x\in\mathfrak g$ and $a,b\in I$; induction starts with
$I=\mathfrak g$. In particular the series is descending, because
$[I,I]\subseteq I$ for every ideal $I$.

The Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ is **solvable** if
$\mathfrak g^{(m)}=0$ for some integer $m\geq0$. Thus the zero Lie algebra is
solvable (take $m=0$), and a nonzero abelian Lie algebra is solvable with
$\mathfrak g^{(1)}=0$. No finite-dimensional or characteristic hypothesis is
part of the definition.

[[thm-murphy-tableau-elements-form-a-cellular-basis]], the local type-A
character theorem [[thm-soergels-character-conjecture]], the singular spherical
formula [[thm-singular-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]],
and the regular-ambient parabolic antispherical formula
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]] retain
their distinct statements and ranges. This route convention introduces no
new theorem, grading, equivalence, or cross-characteristic transfer.

**Parameters.** Let $F$ be a field and $\xi\in F^\times$ with finite quantum
characteristic $e=e(F,\xi)\in\{2,3,\dots\}$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]). We work in
the NONDEGENERATE branch $\xi\ne1$; then $\xi$ is a primitive $e$-th root of
unity in $F$, and all statements on this page live in one of the two
sub-branches: (C0) $\operatorname{char}F=0$, or (CP)
$\operatorname{char}F=p>0$ with $p\nmid e$. The Hecke parameter is written
$\xi$ here; it is the letter $q$ of `def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras`.

**Hecke side.** Fix the level-one fundamental weight $\Lambda_0$ of the cyclic
affine type-$A$ datum with all $d_i=1$ and charge $0$
([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). With the conventions of
`def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras`, $H^\Lambda_d=H_{F,\xi}(S_d)$
is the finite type-$A$ Hecke algebra $T_r^2=(\xi-1)T_r+\xi$
(`prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras`), and
$H^\Lambda_\alpha=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d$ are its residue-content blocks
(`def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks`).

**KLR side.** Use the type-$A$ specialization $Q^A$ of
`def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras` with the same $e$
and the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient
$R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]: the
cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$, induction appends on the
right, and the grading is $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$,
$\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$
([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). The transported grading on
$H^\Lambda_\alpha$ uses a FIXED admissible local normalising series
(`cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading`); a different
series gives a graded-isomorphic transported algebra via $\rho'\rho^{-1}$, and
the graded multiplicities studied below do not depend on the choice.

**Grading and Fock variables.** All grading shifts and all global-basis
polynomials are in the variable $q$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Thus
$\xi\in F^\times$ (the Hecke parameter) and $q$ (the grading variable) are
INDEPENDENT data; the phrase "Ariki's normalization $\xi=q^2$" is retained only
as the source dictionary of [Ariki 1996], whose Hecke parameters are powers of
a square, and no numerical relation or specialization between $\xi$ and $q$ is
imposed.

**Fock side.** Use the level-one symmetric model of
[[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]: charge
$0$, node residues $c-r$, standard vectors $M_\mu$ for ALL partitions $\mu$,
basic/restricted labels the $e$-restricted partitions
$RP_\alpha=\{\lambda:\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<e,\ \operatorname{cont}(\lambda)=\alpha\}$,
empty component $B(\Lambda_0)$. For $\lambda\in RP$ the conjugate $\lambda'$ is
$e$-regular. Write $P(\nu)$ for the independently constructed ordinary
Dipper--James Specht module and $D_{\rm DJ}^{\nu}$ for its form quotient in
`thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell`. Define
$\theta(T_r)=(\xi-1)-T_r=-\xi T_r^{-1}$, the involutive sign automorphism of
[[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. After converting right
modules to left modules through the star anti-involution, the intrinsic
restricted Murphy simple with label $\lambda$ is the $\theta$-pullback of
$D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}$, not the untwisted ordinary module. This is an ungraded
convention dictionary. The pullback can move blocks: on the multiplicative
Jucys--Murphy elements $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$, so charge-zero residue content
is sent from $\alpha$ to $-\alpha$. Thus the ordinary module before pullback has
the conjugate content; no claim identifies it untwisted inside the same block.
At $\xi=1$ the separate specialization theorem
`cor-dj-bridge-specialization-and-composition-multiplicity-dictionary`
identifies $\theta$ with sign tensoring over every field; $\xi=1$ remains
outside the present nondegenerate regime.

No choice principle is used.

Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with **finite** quantum characteristic
$e=e(F,q)$, $2\le e<\infty$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), let
$I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ be the residue set with integer residue labels
$0,1,\dots,e-1$, and use the cyclic affine type-A Cartan datum with dominant
weights $P^+$ and pairing $(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$
([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). In the nondegenerate branch the
distinct spectral values of the labels are $q^i$, while in the degenerate
branch they are $i\cdot1_F$ (here $e=\operatorname{char}F$). Fix
$\Lambda\in P^+$ of level $\ell=\sum_{i\in I}(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$ and put
$\lambda_i:=(\Lambda,\alpha_i)\ge0$.

**(NG) Nondegenerate case $q\ne1$.** The **affine Hecke algebra of type
$A_{d-1}$** at parameter $q$ is the unital $F$-algebra $H_d$ with generators
$X_1^{\pm1},\dots,X_d^{\pm1}$ and $T_1,\dots,T_{d-1}$ subject to the relations
$$X_rX_s=X_sX_r,\qquad X_rX_r^{-1}=1,$$
$$T_rX_rT_r=qX_{r+1},\qquad T_rX_s=X_sT_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
$$T_r^2=(q-1)T_r+q,\qquad T_rT_{r+1}T_r=T_{r+1}T_rT_{r+1},\qquad T_rT_s=T_sT_r\quad(|r-s|>1).$$
The **cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is
$$H^\Lambda_d:=H_d\Big/\bigl\langle\textstyle\prod_{i\in I}(X_1-q^i)^{\lambda_i}\bigr\rangle .$$

**(DG) Degenerate case $q=1$** (which forces $\operatorname{char}F=e>0$). The
**degenerate affine Hecke algebra** $H_d$ is the unital $F$-algebra with
generators $x_1,\dots,x_d$ and $s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ subject to the relations
$$x_rx_s=x_sx_r,\qquad s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1,\qquad s_rx_s=x_ss_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$

[[lem-degenerate-affine-hecke-ordered-monomials-form-a-basis]]. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is
$$H^\Lambda_d:=H_d\Big/\bigl\langle\textstyle\prod_{i\in I}(x_1-i)^{\lambda_i}\bigr\rangle .$$

**Conventions and boundary.** Put $H^\Lambda_0=F$; the cyclotomic polynomial is
imposed on the FIRST polynomial generator, and $T_r$ acts on positions

[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]] ($T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$). At level one

simple roots, a KLR datum $Q=(Q_{ij})_{i\ne j}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4), and a
field $k$ placed in degree zero
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]],
[[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]); let
$R=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R(\beta)$ be the resulting graded KLR algebra, with

$\deg x_a=2d_{\nu_a}$, $\deg\tau_a=-b_{\nu_a\nu_{a+1}}$
([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). Let $\Lambda$ be a
dominant integral weight and put $\lambda_i:=\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle\ge0$
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

**Cyclotomic data.** For every color $i$ choose a monic polynomial
$a_i(u)\in k[u]$ of degree exactly $\lambda_i$
([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]); the standard choice made
below is $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. For $n\ge1$ write
$$a(x_s)=\sum_{\nu\in I^n}a_{\nu_s}(x_s)e(\nu)\qquad(1\le s\le n),$$
the element of $R_n(Q)$ that acts on the $\nu$-component by the monic
polynomial $a_{\nu_s}$ in the dot at position $s$.

**The cyclotomic quotient.** For $\beta\in Q_+$ define $J_a(\beta)$ to be the
two-sided ideal of $R(\beta)$ generated by the first-strand elements
$a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)$, $\nu\in I^\beta$; equivalently
$$J_a(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}R(\beta)\,a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)\,R(\beta),$$
and put
$$R_a^\Lambda(\beta):=R(\beta)/J_a(\beta),\qquad R_a^\Lambda(0):=k .$$
The **cyclotomic KLR algebra** is the direct sum
$R_a^\Lambda:=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$; it carries the
local units $e(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu)$, which act as the identity
on $R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$ and annihilate the other summands, and it is a
$k$-algebra with these orthogonal idempotents.

**Standard choice and grading.** The STANDARD choice $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$ is
used throughout the graded categorification, duality-normalization and based
statements below; for it we write $R^\Lambda:=R^\Lambda_a$. Under the standard
choice each individual first-strand generator
$x_1^{\lambda_{\nu_1}}e(\nu)$ is homogeneous of degree
$2d_{\nu_1}\lambda_{\nu_1}$ in the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], so the ideal $J_a(\beta)$
and the quotient $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ are graded, and $R^\Lambda$ is a
$\mathbb Z$-graded algebra with local units. The sum $a(x_1)$ itself need not
have one common degree across different colors, and no single degree is
assigned to it.

**Boundary of the definition.** Arbitrary monic polynomials with lower
coefficients in degree-zero $k$ give an UNGRADED deformation $R_a^\Lambda$;
nilpotent dots, homogeneous trace degree and the highest-weight graded $K_0$
identification are not asserted for that branch, and the ungraded branch is
used only where a statement explicitly says so. Finite dimension, finite root
strings, ordinary projectivity and symmetry of the standard quotient have the
separately stated monic conclusions below. The cyclotomic relation is imposed
on the FIRST strand, and cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT
([[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]); this convention
fixes the side on which the quotient map acts throughout the page.

[[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]]. By
[[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-polynomial-spectra-and-central-content-sectors]],
$H^\Lambda_d$ is finite-dimensional and each minimal polynomial of the
polynomial generator $z_r=X_r$ (nondegenerate normalization) respectively
$x_r$ (degenerate normalization) splits over the residues $c_i=q_H^i$
respectively $i\cdot1_F$.

**Residue-sequence idempotents.** Let $\varepsilon_r(i)$ be the canonical CRT
primary idempotent of that generator at the spectral value $c_i$ associated with residue label $i$ (zero when that value is
absent), and put
$$e(\nu)=\prod_{r=1}^{d}\varepsilon_r(\nu_r)$$
for a residue sequence $\nu=(\nu_1,\dots,\nu_d)\in(\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z)^d$. On
every finite $H$-module the element $e(\nu)$ projects onto the joint
generalized residue space, and these mutually orthogonal idempotents sum to
$1$. At content $\alpha$ put
$$e_\alpha=\sum_{\nu\in I_\alpha}e(\nu),$$
the sum over residue sequences of content $\alpha$; it is central, and
$H^\Lambda_d$ is the direct sum of its central ideals
$$H^\Lambda_\alpha=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d\,e_\alpha.$$
By
[[thm-cyclotomic-hecke-central-content-sectors-are-zero-or-primitive-blocks]],
every nonzero $e_\alpha$ is primitive, so every nonzero $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is
an actual block
([[def-blocks-of-a-finite-dimensional-algebra-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]);
this block assertion is proved there, not retained as an unused citation.
The algebra basis and dimension convention is that of
[[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra-basis-and-dimension]].

**Level one.** At level one, $\Lambda=\Lambda_j$, the polynomial generators
correspond under the explicit finite-Hecke inverse of
[[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]] to
$$X_r=q_H^j\bigl(1+(q_H-1)L_r\bigr)\quad\text{(nondegenerate)},\qquad x_r=j+L_r\quad\text{(degenerate)},$$
where $L_r$ is the ordinary additive Jucys–Murphy element. Thus on a standard
tableau node of content $m$ their eigenvalues are $q_H^{j+m}$ respectively
$j+m$, while $L_r$ itself has additive $q$-content $[m]_{q_H}$. The nonzero
joint projectors are precisely the residue words of standard tableaux
([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]]), and grouping
those words by content gives the block labels.

**Boundary conventions.** At rank zero the empty projector is $1$ and the
unique block is $F$; at level zero and positive rank all projectors and blocks
are zero. The projection, centrality, and block-decomposition assertions
recorded here are exactly the proved content-sector statements of the linked
suppliers; this definition introduces no new primitive-block classification
of its own. It uses no choice principle: all spectra, projectors, and sums are
finite.

Let $F$ be any field, let $q\in F^\times$ have finite quantum characteristic
$e=e(F,q)\ge2$, let $\Lambda\in P^+$ be dominant and let $\alpha\in Q_+$ have
height $d$ with $e_\alpha\ne0$, in the conventions of
[[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]] and
[[def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks]]. Then the
homomorphisms $\rho\colon R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ of
[[lem-hecke-intertwiners-produce-local-klr-generators]] and
$\sigma\colon H^\Lambda_\alpha\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of
[[lem-cyclotomic-klr-block-satisfies-the-hecke-relations]] are mutually
inverse $F$-algebra isomorphisms. Equivalently, $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is
generated by the Khovanov–Lauda generators
$\{e(i)\}\cup\{y_r\}\cup\{\psi_r\}$ subject only to the relations
(1.6)–(1.15), and the isomorphism is normalized by
$\rho(e(i))=e(i)$ and
$$\rho(y_re(i))=(1-q^{-i_r}X_r)e(i)\quad(q\ne1),\qquad \rho(y_re(i))=(x_r-i_r)e(i)\quad(q=1).$$
The degenerate ($q=1$, $\operatorname{char}F=e$) and nondegenerate
($q\ne1$) cases are proved separately, and both hold in finite quantum
characteristic $e$.

This page uses the following **route convention**. Category O means the BGG
category for a fixed finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra and a
chosen positive system, as defined in [[def-bgg-category-o]]. The
Arakawa–Suzuki route is the *degenerate affine* route over $\mathbb C$: on
$M\otimes (\mathbb C^N)^{\otimes d}$ use the operators $x_j$ and $s_i$ of
[[def-arakawa-suzuki-casimir-operators-on-tensor-functors]], with the verified
right $H_d$-action of
[[thm-the-casimir-and-place-permutation-operators-satisfy-degenerate-affine-hecke-relations]].
The source-normalized operators are
$$y_j=x_j-\frac{1}{N}z_M+\frac{N-1}{2};$$
they are not new generators to be identified with a nondegenerate Hecke
generator. Here $z_M$ is the central endomorphism specified in the cited
definition. This convention asserts no extension of the cited hypotheses on
$M$, origin, or tensor functor.

The finite cyclic type-A Hecke/KLR route uses a field $F$, a finite quantum
characteristic $e\ge2$, and its declared residue and cyclotomic conventions
([[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]]). In the nondegenerate
branch write the Hecke parameter as $\xi\ne1$ and reserve $q$ for the grading
and Laurent-polynomial variable. The blockwise identification is exactly
[[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]]: write
$\xi_{\mathrm{BK}}$ for its Hecke parameter (denoted $q$ in that theorem),
independent of the grading variable $q$. Its $\xi_{\mathrm{BK}}=1$ branch
requires $\operatorname{char}F=e$, while its $\xi_{\mathrm{BK}}\ne1$ branch is
separate. For
level-one Ariki statements, use only the regime in
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]]. In characteristic
zero the canonical-basis and graded-decomposition conclusions are those of
[[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] and
[[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]].
In positive characteristic retain the adjustment factorization of
[[thm-positive-characteristic-decomposition-polynomials-factor-through-adjustment]];
no identity adjustment matrix is part of this route.

The negative-half KLR categorification and the cyclotomic highest-weight
projective-$K_0$ theorem are distinct routes, respectively
[[thm-klr-categorification-of-the-negative-quantum-half]] and
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]].
Each keeps its own field, grading, weight and Axiom-of-Choice hypotheses
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
Likewise, the type-A Hecke cellular result
[[thm-murphy-tableau-elements-form-a-cellular-basis]], the local type-A
character theorem [[thm-soergels-character-conjecture]], the singular spherical
formula [[thm-singular-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]],
and the regular-ambient parabolic antispherical formula
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]] retain
their distinct statements and ranges. This route convention introduces no
new theorem, grading, equivalence, or cross-characteristic transfer.

**Parameters.** Let $F$ be a field and $\xi\in F^\times$ with finite quantum
characteristic $e=e(F,\xi)\in\{2,3,\dots\}$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]). We work in
the NONDEGENERATE branch $\xi\ne1$; then $\xi$ is a primitive $e$-th root of
unity in $F$, and all statements on this page live in one of the two
sub-branches: (C0) $\operatorname{char}F=0$, or (CP)
$\operatorname{char}F=p>0$ with $p\nmid e$. The Hecke parameter is written
$\xi$ here; it is the letter $q$ of `def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras`.

**Hecke side.** Fix the level-one fundamental weight $\Lambda_0$ of the cyclic
affine type-$A$ datum with all $d_i=1$ and charge $0$
([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). With the conventions of
`def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras`, $H^\Lambda_d=H_{F,\xi}(S_d)$
is the finite type-$A$ Hecke algebra $T_r^2=(\xi-1)T_r+\xi$
(`prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras`), and
$H^\Lambda_\alpha=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d$ are its residue-content blocks
(`def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks`).

**KLR side.** Use the type-$A$ specialization $Q^A$ of
`def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras` with the same $e$
and the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient
$R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]: the
cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$, induction appends on the
right, and the grading is $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$,
$\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$
([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). The transported grading on
$H^\Lambda_\alpha$ uses a FIXED admissible local normalising series
(`cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading`); a different
series gives a graded-isomorphic transported algebra via $\rho'\rho^{-1}$, and
the graded multiplicities studied below do not depend on the choice.

**Grading and Fock variables.** All grading shifts and all global-basis
polynomials are in the variable $q$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Thus
$\xi\in F^\times$ (the Hecke parameter) and $q$ (the grading variable) are
INDEPENDENT data; the phrase "Ariki's normalization $\xi=q^2$" is retained only
as the source dictionary of [Ariki 1996], whose Hecke parameters are powers of
a square, and no numerical relation or specialization between $\xi$ and $q$ is
imposed.

**Fock side.** Use the level-one symmetric model of
[[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]: charge
$0$, node residues $c-r$, standard vectors $M_\mu$ for ALL partitions $\mu$,
basic/restricted labels the $e$-restricted partitions
$RP_\alpha=\{\lambda:\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<e,\ \operatorname{cont}(\lambda)=\alpha\}$,
empty component $B(\Lambda_0)$. For $\lambda\in RP$ the conjugate $\lambda'$ is
$e$-regular. Write $P(\nu)$ for the independently constructed ordinary
Dipper--James Specht module and $D_{\rm DJ}^{\nu}$ for its form quotient in
`thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell`. Define
$\theta(T_r)=(\xi-1)-T_r=-\xi T_r^{-1}$, the involutive sign automorphism of
[[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. After converting right
modules to left modules through the star anti-involution, the intrinsic
restricted Murphy simple with label $\lambda$ is the $\theta$-pullback of
$D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}$, not the untwisted ordinary module. This is an ungraded
convention dictionary. The pullback can move blocks: on the multiplicative
Jucys--Murphy elements $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$, so charge-zero residue content
is sent from $\alpha$ to $-\alpha$. Thus the ordinary module before pullback has
the conjugate content; no claim identifies it untwisted inside the same block.
At $\xi=1$ the separate specialization theorem
`cor-dj-bridge-specialization-and-composition-multiplicity-dictionary`
identifies $\theta$ with sign tensoring over every field; $\xi=1$ remains
outside the present nondegenerate regime.

No choice principle is used.

Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with **finite** quantum characteristic
$e=e(F,q)$, $2\le e<\infty$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), let
$I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ be the residue set with integer residue labels
$0,1,\dots,e-1$, and use the cyclic affine type-A Cartan datum with dominant
weights $P^+$ and pairing $(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$
([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). In the nondegenerate branch the
distinct spectral values of the labels are $q^i$, while in the degenerate
branch they are $i\cdot1_F$ (here $e=\operatorname{char}F$). Fix
$\Lambda\in P^+$ of level $\ell=\sum_{i\in I}(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$ and put
$\lambda_i:=(\Lambda,\alpha_i)\ge0$.

**(NG) Nondegenerate case $q\ne1$.** The **affine Hecke algebra of type
$A_{d-1}$** at parameter $q$ is the unital $F$-algebra $H_d$ with generators
$X_1^{\pm1},\dots,X_d^{\pm1}$ and $T_1,\dots,T_{d-1}$ subject to the relations
$$X_rX_s=X_sX_r,\qquad X_rX_r^{-1}=1,$$
$$T_rX_rT_r=qX_{r+1},\qquad T_rX_s=X_sT_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
$$T_r^2=(q-1)T_r+q,\qquad T_rT_{r+1}T_r=T_{r+1}T_rT_{r+1},\qquad T_rT_s=T_sT_r\quad(|r-s|>1).$$
The **cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is
$$H^\Lambda_d:=H_d\Big/\bigl\langle\textstyle\prod_{i\in I}(X_1-q^i)^{\lambda_i}\bigr\rangle .$$

**(DG) Degenerate case $q=1$** (which forces $\operatorname{char}F=e>0$). The
**degenerate affine Hecke algebra** $H_d$ is the unital $F$-algebra with
generators $x_1,\dots,x_d$ and $s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ subject to the relations
$$x_rx_s=x_sx_r,\qquad s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1,\qquad s_rx_s=x_ss_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
$$s_r^2=1,\qquad s_rs_{r+1}s_r=s_{r+1}s_rs_{r+1},\qquad s_rs_t=s_ts_r\quad(|r-t|>1);$$
its ordered monomials $x_1^{m_1}\cdots x_d^{m_d}w$ form an $F$-basis by
[[lem-degenerate-affine-hecke-ordered-monomials-form-a-basis]]. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is
$$H^\Lambda_d:=H_d\Big/\bigl\langle\textstyle\prod_{i\in I}(x_1-i)^{\lambda_i}\bigr\rangle .$$

**Conventions and boundary.** Put $H^\Lambda_0=F$; the cyclotomic polynomial is
imposed on the FIRST polynomial generator, and $T_r$ acts on positions
$r,r+1$. The Hecke parameter is the one of
[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]] ($T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$). At level one
$\Lambda=\Lambda_j$, the algebra $H^\Lambda_d$ is the finite type-A Hecke
algebra $H_{F,q}(S_d)$ if $q\ne1$ and the group algebra $FS_d$ if $q=1$
([[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]).
Only finite $e$ is treated: the source's $e=0$ branches ($q$ not a root of
unity, and the characteristic-zero degeneration, whose quiver is $A_\infty$)
are outside this page's cyclic scope and are recorded as a deferred boundary in
the batch notes. These presentations and the charged quotients are the ones of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]]; no
embedding of the label set $I$ into $F$ is claimed in the nondegenerate branch,
and no choice principle is used.

Work over $\mathbb C$ ([[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]],
[[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). Fix $N\ge1$, let
$\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ with its matrix units $E_{ij}$ and the
trace form $B(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}(XY)$, which is symmetric, nondegenerate and
invariant ([[prop-trace-forms-are-symmetric-and-invariant]]), and let
$$z:=\sum_{i=1}^NE_{ii}\in\mathfrak g$$
be the central element (the identity matrix). The dual basis of $(E_{ij})$
under $B$ is $(E_{ji})$, so the invariant Casimir tensor is
$$\Omega=\sum_{i,j=1}^NE_{ij}\otimes E_{ji}\in U(\mathfrak g)\otimes U(\mathfrak g),$$
Its action on a tensor product of two $\mathfrak g$-modules commutes with the diagonal action, as computed in [F2]. Multiplying its two factors gives the central Casimir element of [[def-casimir-operator-relative-to-an-invariant-form]].

Let $M$ be a $\mathfrak g$-module and $V=\mathbb C^N$ the natural module
([[def-representation-of-a-lie-algebra]]). On the tensor product
$M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]],
[[thm-associativity-of-balanced-tensor-products]]) label the factors
$0,1,\dots,d$, with factor $0$ equal to $M$. For $0\le a\ne b\le d$ let
$\Omega_{ab}$ denote the operator obtained by applying $\Omega$ in the two
labelled factors, and for distinct $1\le a,b\le d$ let $P_{ab}$ denote the
operator that interchanges the two labelled factors (the flip of
$V\otimes V$ on two $V$-factors). Define, for $1\le j\le d$ and
$1\le i\le d-1$,
$$x_j:=\Omega_{0j}+\sum_{k<j}P_{kj},\qquad s_i:=P_{i,i+1}.$$
Finally put $\Omega^{\mathrm{sl}}:=\Omega-\tfrac1Nz\otimes z$ and define the
Arakawa-Suzuki normalized operators
$$y_j:=x_j-\tfrac1Nz_M+\tfrac{N-1}{2},$$
where $z_M$ denotes the endomorphism of $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ given by the
action of $z$ on the factor $M$. This is a central endomorphism, and is a scalar only when $z$ acts scalarly on $M$.

The verification below records the properties of these operators used on this
page: $\Omega$ acts on $V\otimes V$ as the flip; the operators $x_j$ and
$s_i$ are natural in $M$ and commute with the $\mathfrak g$-action; the
recursion $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$ holds; $\Omega^{\mathrm{sl}}$ is the Casimir
of $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ relative to the restricted trace form; and the operators
$y_j$ are exactly the source operators of [AS, (2.2.2)]. For $d=0$ the family
$(x_j)$ is empty; for the trivial module $M=\mathbb C$ one has $\Omega_{0j}=0$,
so $x_j=\sum_{k<j}P_{kj}$ and $x_1=0$.

Let $N\ge1$, let $M$ be a $\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$-module, let
$V=\mathbb C^N$ be the natural module, and on $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ use the
operators $x_j=\Omega_{0j}+\sum_{k<j}P_{kj}$ and $s_i=P_{i,i+1}$ of
[[def-arakawa-suzuki-casimir-operators-on-tensor-functors]]. Then:

1. The operators $x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ commute with the
   $\mathfrak g$-action and are natural in $M$, and satisfy all the defining
   relations of the degenerate affine Hecke algebra
   [[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]]: the Coxeter relations for the
   $s_i$; $s_ix_j=x_js_i$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$; $s_ix_{i+1}=x_is_i+1$ and
   $x_{i+1}s_i=s_ix_i+1$; and the polynomial commutation $[x_i,x_j]=0$.
2. Consequently they define, via the generator-fixing anti-involution of the
   Hecke algebra, a natural right $H_d$-action on $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$
   commuting with the left $\mathfrak g$-action.

The commutation of the $x_i$ is an independent check: it does not follow from
the braid relations of the $s_i$ alone.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring. If $M$ is free with basis $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ and $N$ is free with basis $(f_j)_{j\in J}$, then $M\otimes_RN$ is free with basis

$$\bigl(e_i\otimes f_j\bigr)_{(i,j)\in I\times J}.$$

Equivalently, the canonical map $R^{(I\times J)}\to M\otimes_RN$ sending the standard basis vector at $(i,j)$ to $e_i\otimes f_j$ is an isomorphism. This includes an empty basis in either factor.
